doc.title: Chico Hamilton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 30, 2000

title: Starting a commercials production company
summary: He composed and produced jingles for IBM, Revlon, Chrysler, Volkswagen and others.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: That’s right. In 1966 you started a production company?

Yeah. I was doing commercials. It was very successful. Very successful. As a matter of fact I would say during that part of the 60s some of the best music on television was the commercial music, because they were using jazz, a lot of jazz.
Can you mention a few commercials that—

That I did? Sure. The first time IBM ever went on the air they had three minute spots, which was considered a feature. I did all the music for IBM. I did the music for Revlon, Chrysler, Volkswagen. My first commercial that I ever did was when cigarettes were on the air, Spring Cigarettes. [sings] Spring is better. I did that. I had that whole campaign. Ivory Soap [scats] I did that. It was very successful. I reached a point though that I got tapped out. I reached a point that I was doing everything for the money. It didn’t matter what it was. And you start pigeon-holing things. And one day man I was at a meeting, a big meeting, and not only was I the composer and arranger but I was the producer as well. And as a producer man, I’m handling accounts at that time, maybe a quarter of a million dollars account, that kind of money that was going to be spent in regards to that.
